cells.reference: ARE, 1905, no. 105; SII. XIV, no. 13, pp. 9-10; EI. IX, No. 10 p. 84 ff.
cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xiv||13" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XIV, No. 13</button>
cells.remarks: Records gift of 290 kāsū by king Varaguna Mahārāja for worship and food offerings 4 times a day to the Śrīkōil-Bhaṭārar of Ilaṅgōykkuđi. The amount was entrusted to the Sabhā of Ilaṅgōykkuđi who were to measure out two kalam of paddy per kāsū as interest to the temple. Items composing food offerings for each item were as shown below :— Senneltittal rice (4 nālis); green dal for Kummāyam; Ghee (ulakku); curds (1 uṛi); four plantain; Sugar (1 palam) vegetables (kaṛi-amirdu); Kāykari (one) and ghee ; curds and so for (2 sevidu) for kūṭtu; betel (2 bundles), areca nuts (forty), lime (1 sevidu). It is recorded that this gift was made to the temple while the king Varaguṇa Mahārāja was camping at Ara śur on the banks of the river Peṇnai in Toṇdaināđu.

cells.king: Pāndya Vīra-Pāndyadēva 'who took the head of the Chōla'
cells.date: r.y. 5th year opposite to the 15th year = c. A.D. 967
cells.reference: ARE, 1905, no. 101 ; SII, XIV, no. 85, pp. 60-61, EI. XXV, no. 6, pp. 35 ff.
cells.remarks: The inscription confirms an earlier royal order dated in the 12th year of Vīrapāndya on the occasion of the solar eclipse in the month of Mithuṇa, granting 10 vēli of land as kudinīngā-dēvadāna to the temple of Tiruppōttuđaiya-Mahādēva at Ilaṅgōykkuđi, a brahmadēya in Mulli-nāđu for provision of worship and offerings to the different deities in the temple. The provisions included rice, vegetables, cost of maintenance of potters, washermen, carpenters, drummers and other officials in the temple service at different rates. A portion of the land was earmarked as Tiruvilāppuram Tirumelukkuppuram and Pudukkuppuram. An officer of the king named Chōlāntaka Brahmamārāyar and another named Tamilavēlān figure in the record.

cells.remarks: Records gift of the village Sokkaṇkuļam, the eastern hamlet of Rājarāja-Chaturvēdimaṅgalam, for maintaining lamps in the temple of Arikēsariśvaramuḍaiya Nāyaṇār at Arikēsarinallūr in Mulli-nāḍu. The gift was made at the suggestion of Kālīṅgarāyar, by the king's younger brother Tirunelvēli Bhagavati Aļagapperumāļ alias Kulasēkhara-Kaṇḍiyadēvar who was also the donor of the lamps. The document is signed by Tirunelvēli-uḍaiyān alias Toṇḍaimāṇ and two others. The assembly of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in the presence of Nālāyira-Mūvēndavēlāṇ and Rāja-nārāyaṇa-Mūvēndavēlāṇ carried out the royal orders fixing the assessment at 3 achchu per year and excluded the granted lands from the vari-register.

Registers the gift of half of a vēli of land at Mēlkuppāyakkuđi to the shrines of Maṇavāļa-Ālvār alias Nilaimai-Alāgiya Perumāl and Narasiimha-Ālvar, in the temple of Jayatoṅga-Viṇnagar Ālvār, at Vađatalaikkaļam, the north-eastern hamlet of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimaṅgalam. The king's order to make the gift was executed and the document engraved on stone. The first of the shrine was built by Pađiyāñi Bhagavati alias Kaṇđiyadēva of Tirunelvēli.

cells.remarks: It is stated that at the time of giving this order the Chōla-Pāṇdya-viceroy was seated in the western hall of the open ground for conducting dances (āttattuveli) in the palace. Records some lands sold to the temple of Rājēndrachōla-viṇṇagar-Dēvar by the sabhā of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimaṅgalam were converted from brahmadēya to veḥlāṇvagai from the 13th year of the king and the taxes levied on them in kind and cash were asked to be paid to the temple. From that year the taxes alagerudukāṭchi-kāśu, kāṭchi-erudu-kāśu and ūrkkalaṇju were remitted on them to make them tax-free dēvadāna. Necessary entries were made in tax-registers by the king's officers. Note : The inscription is related to Tn. 138 ; No. 109 of 1905 ; SII. XIV, no. 144.

cells.remarks: The Śrīvaishnavas of Rājēndra-Viṇnagar in Rājarāja-Chaturvēdimaṅgalam granted to Cheṇdalaṅkāradāsar, a pīdipādu under the following circumstances. The latter having got the release of certain lands in Vindanūr alias Avanimārtānđapuram the ownership of which was disputed by the residents of Puliyūr in Teṇvāri-nāđu and of Śrīvallabha-chaturvēdimaṅglam in Kurumarai-nāđu in the boundary dispute referred to in an inscription of the same village (ARE. No. 400, 1916), the nagarattār of Vindanūr granted the Kārāṇmai of these lands Cheṇdalankāradāsar of Kulāśēkhara-Perumāļ shrine. The king on the occasion of his presence at the Nālāyiravaṇ-tirumaṇđapam to hear the tiruppāvai, remitted all the taxes on these lands including kadamai and antarāyam.

cells.king: Māravarman alias Tribhuvanachakravartin Sundara-Pāṇdyadēva, (Sundara Pāṇdya I), 'who took the Chōla country and performed the anointment of heroes at Muđikoṇđa-Chōlapuram'
cells.remarks: Records that the members of the village (Ūr) who performed the Sēnāpatittaṇam and daṇdanāyakam and the tandirattār who belonged to the parikkirāgam of Kōnāđu-Kađayam alias Vikrama-Pāṇdyanallūr, gave their maintenance (jivita) lands under Āṇdarkuļam to Daśaratha-Rāmiśvarmuđaiyār in the temple of Śrī-Kailāsam of that village in order that the worship and offerings to the several gods and goddesses set up by them in the temple may be conducted. In doing this, the temple was required to pay some money to three different mortgagees and to get the release of the lands. The donors agreed to pay iñjadu and variñjadu on these lands by reserving for themselves one kalam of paddy on each mā of wetland on which crops had been raised.

cells.reference: ARE, 1916, no. 539 ; Ibid., part II, para. 10.
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction 'tirumagaṭ jayamagaṭ' etc. of the inscriptions of the king. Registers that the assembly of Chēramādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam assigned a portion of a land already in the enjoyment of temple in lieu of another which they had granted to the temple on the occasion of its foundation, the latter being disputed to have been the gift of another Vishnu temple in the same village, called Śrīvallabha-Viṇṇagar. In consideration of this new transaction and exchange the assembly gave some money to the temple and declared that the land now given was to be a dēvadāna of the temple.

cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xiv||157" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XIV, No. 157</button>
cells.remarks: Registers royal order by the king for the gift of 2 vēlis of land in the village of Kallūr in Mēlvēmbanāđu Muḍikonḍachōļa-vaļanāđu to the temple of Śrīkailāsamuḍaiyāṇ Mahādēva at the instance of his maternal uncle (ammāṇ). The land was separated from the original entry in the register and made into a new unit called Śīvapādaśēkhara-nallur which was entered in the tax-register duly from the 16th year of the ruler. The kāṭchi-kāśu and kāṭchierudu-kāśu and ūrkkaļañju. Note : The present record is a fine example of the conversional methods adopted for preparing land-gift documents with meticulous details. cells.remarks: Records that when the viceroy was in his palace at Rājēndra-chōlapuram, he received the communciation from his father (nam-ayyar) who had the meykirti beginning with 'vīramē-tuṇaiyāgavum' asking the former to grant 4 vēli lands, as tax-free, dēvadāna to the temple of Kayilāsamuđaiya-Mahādēva situated on the south bank of Muđikoṇđa-chōla-pērāru at Nigarili-chōla-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in Mullī-nāđu, a s.d. of Uttama-chōla-vaļanāđu. According to the viceroy gave orders to his officers that these lands situated at Kallūr, in Mēl-vēmba-nāđu of Muđikoṇđa-chōlavaļanāđu be converted from Vellāṇ-vagai to tax-free from the 3rd year and be clubbed with the adjacent Śivapādašēkhara-nallūr, already a dēvadāna of the temple, to make them one village and one revenue unit (ōrūrāy-orupuravāy). Consequently the taxes irai, ūrk-kālaṇju and antarāyam including of Kumarak-kachchāṇam, taṇi-irai, taṭṭārp-pāṭtam and packaval-kuļi, exempted on the lands amounting to 32 kāśu 567 kalam of paddy should be paid to the temple for provision of various services. The officers of the Department of revenue entered scrupulously the various details in the tax-registers in the 2nd year and 388th day of the king.

cells.reference: ARE, 1911, no. 544; Ibid., part II, para. 38
cells.remarks: Registers the grant mentioned in a 15th year inscription of the king on the north wall Tn 315 ; (540 of 1911) and perhaps also another gift of land to supplement it, at the instance of the assembly of Šēravaṇ-mahādēvi chaturvēdimaṅgalam. cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xiv||160" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XIV, No. 160</button>
cells.remarks: Records gift of 5 vēli of land by purchase from the sabhā of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimaṅgalam for the daily expenses for conducting festivals and for feeding 25 brāhmaṇas and the person who read Śivadharma, in the temple of Tiruvālīśvaramuḍaiya-Mahādēva. The land which was a brahmadēya was converted into vellāṇvagai before making the gift. The king is stated to have been seated in the western pavilion in the āṭattuveļi in the palace precincts at Rājēndra-chōlapuram at the time of this grant. The gift was made by the king at the instance of his maternal uncle (ammāṇ). The record mentions a number of officials who made the necessary entries in the tax-register. Note: It is to be noted that 5 kāśu was levied towards the tax—kāchi-erudu-kāśu which was usually remitted on temple lands. See also Tn. 353; SII. XIV, No. 161 from the same place.

cells.remarks: Records that when some lands, brought from the sabhā of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, a brahmadēya of Mulli-nādu Muḍikonḍa-chōla-valanādu and granted to the temple of Tiruvālīśvaramuḍaiyār by the king at the instance of his uncle (ammāṇ), were entered in the tax-register, the particulars concerning the boundaries of the lands were wrongly entered that the defect was rectified by making fresh and correct entries. The original entry was made in the 16th year of king Tn. 352; (SII. XVI, no. 160) and the fresh entry was made in the 17th year and 65th day of the reign of the same king. The defect was brought to the king's notice in the 17th year and 53rd day when he was seated in the dining hall on the seat called Rājēndra-chōla-Atimūrkach-cheṅgīrai in the chitrakūḍām in the flower-garden called Puttan to the north of Madurai Māḍakkulak-kīl, a sub-division of Madhurāntaka-valandādu.

cells.language: Tamil in Tamil characters, 186 lines, partly damaged
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction “Tirumaga! jayamaga!” etc. of the inscriptions of the king. Records the order of the king granting Śivacharaṇaśēkharanallūr, a free dēvadāna from the 17th year of the king to the temple Tiruvāliśvaram-Uđaiyār at Rājarāja-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in Mulli-nāđu. The granted village was newly constituted of—vēli of lands that lay comprised by the first eight Kaṇṇār to the south of a channel called Vāśudēva-vāykkāl in the above village. One Mantiri Pūvaṇ alias Mānābharaṇa Uttaramantiri figures as one of the mugaveṭtis endorsing the document. Ten mā of land out of the donated lands had been previously granted by a lady, Umaiyammai as tiruvilākkuppuram to the temple. The endowment was entrusted, at the instance of Sēnāpatigaļ Rājarāja Veļlappa Nādāļvār, to Šańkarappāđiyān Mānābharaṇa Vaikunta Nādāļvān and his line. The record was engraved on by Parākrama-Pāndya-Perundachchaṇ. Note: Mānābharaṇn, found as part of the names of Utaramantri and Sańkarappāđiyān, was the name of a son of Jatāvarman Śrivallabha whose records begin with the historical introduction “Tirumađandaiyum jayamađandaiyum”, etc. of the inscriptions of the king. (Tn.....; SII. XIV, no. 225 Rājaśingamaṇdalam). Hence it may be suggested that Śrivallabha of the present record is identical with above).

Note: Mānābharaṇn, found as part of the names of Utaramantri and Sańkarappāđiyān, was the name of a son of Jatāvarman Śrivallabha whose records begin with the historical introduction “Tirumađandaiyum jayamađandaiyum”, etc. of the inscriptions of the king. (Tn.....; SII. XIV, no. 225 Rājaśingamaṇdalam). Hence it may be suggested that Śrivallabha of the present record is identical with above).

cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="are" data-key="are|1915-17|g|215" data-url="ARE-Inscriptions.html">ARE 1915-17, App. G, No. 483</button>
cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction 'pūmaruviya tirumađandaiym' etc. of the inscriptions of the king. The king being seated on his throne Maļavarāyan in his palace at Madurai to the east of Māđakkuļam in Mādurōdaya Vaļanāđu, ordered at the request of Maļavarāyan that some lands be given as tax-free dēvadāna with all income to the temple of Tiruvākkiśvaramuđaiyār at Vaļudiyūr, the north-eastern hamlet of Rājarāja-chaturvēdimaņgalam. It was also ordered by Tribhuvanachakravartin Kōnēriņ-maikoņdāņ (i.e. the king). in the 15th year and 405th day that the grant may be registered in the books and a copy of the order furnished (variyilār eļuttiţta uļvariyum kēļviyum tarachchoņņōm). The registry was also made in the same year and the record was egraved evidently on the 542nd day after the 15th year.

cells.remarks: The king being seated on his throne called Muṇaiyadarayaṇ in his palace at Erikkitṭūr, alias Śrivallabhapaṭṭiṇam in Kīl-Chembilnādu, ordered the grant of a quarter vēli of land at Kudurai-cṛṭi, after making the necessary entries in the revenue registers (uļvari). The land was also exempted from antarāya as per verbal orders passed in the 4th year and the 992nd day, by the king when he was seated on his throne Muṇaiyadaraiyaṇ in the Śrīvallabhaṇ-hall within the palace at Madurai to the east of Māđakkuļam. The entries in the uļvari register regarding the antarāyam exemption are next entered.

cells.reference: ARE, 1908, no. 43; SII. XIV. no. 31, p. 26; TAS. I. pp. 3-4
cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="are" data-key="are|1906-10|c|1204" data-url="ARE-Inscriptions.html">ARE 1906-10, App. C, No. 43</button>; <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xiv||31" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XIV, No. 31</button>
cells.match_text: ARE 1906-10, App. C, No. 43; SII Vol. XIV, No. 31
cells.remarks: The record refers to an expedition of the Pāṇdya army, under the command of Eṭti-Maṇṇaṇ alias Mangaĵa Eṇādi, against Śadayaṇ Karunandaṇ of Malaināđu in which the fort of Aruviyār was destroyed. The inscription registers a gift of land valued at 21 kalaṇju of gold by the commander to the sabhā of Guṇamangalam on behalf of Viṇaiyantoĵu-Sūraṇ of Pūndanmali in Toṇdai-nāđu and Sāttanakkaṇ of Pēreyir kuđi who died in the above battle. NOTE: According to the Epigraphists, Śadaiyaṇ Karunandaṇ is identical with the Āy chieftain of the same name whose records are found in the northern region of the old Travancore State. His title Śadaiyaṇ indicates that he might have been a feudatory of the Pāṇdya king who had subsequently become independent with the help of Vēnāđu rulers.

cells.reference: ARE, 1929, no. 12; SII. XIV, no. 40, pp. 30-31
cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xiv||40" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XIV, No. 40</button>
cells.remarks: Registers two separate endowments by a certain Vēlāñ of Irumbāđu in Karaikkāṇa-nāđu. One was a gift of 50 sheep to maintain a lamp in the rest house called Rājakkattannirpperumbandal erected by him at Perumbaļañji in Nāttārrup-pōkku. Some land and a well were also provided for it. The other gift of sheep was for maintaining a lamp in another rest-house named Munnūrruvañ-perumbandal set up by him in the village. A gift of land was also provided for the care-taker who supplied water to this water-shed. The Nāyakaṇniār ruling the district were charged with the protection of these gifts.

cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction "Tirumađandaiyum Jayamađandaiyum" etc. of the inscriptions of the king. The record refers to some transaction made in the 31st year of Kulōttuṅgachōladēva, 'who took Kollam', relating to the temple of Varaguṇa-Vainṇagarālyvār, Saṭhagōpa-Viṇnagarālyvār and Śrī Rāghava Chakravartigal. NOTE: Śaṅkaraṇ Vāśudēvaṇ was a subordinate officer of Iravi-Kōdai, the ruler of Vēṇāđu (Tn 652 SII. XIV, no. 231, from the same place).

cells.remarks: Begins with the historical introduction "Tirumađandaiyum Jayamađandaiyum" etc. of the inscriptions of the king. Refers to the breaching of the tank called Maṇōmayaṇēri at Vijayanārāyaṇa-chaturvēdimaṅgalam and to its being closed by a certain Nambi Śaṅkaraṇ Vāśudēvaṇ of Turuttimaṅgalam. He was in charge of the village under Iravi Kōdaivarman, the ruler of Vēṇāđu. He also made an endowment of land for the annual repair of the tank. The channel was repaired by the same donor name as Vāśudēvappērāru. NOTE: It is interesting to note that the Vēṇāđu ruler Ravi Kōdai was a contemporary of Jaṭāvarman Śrīvallabha.

cells.remarks: Pāṇdya ; Jaṭāvarman Tribhuvana-chakravartin Kulasēkharadēva, (Kulasēkhara I), r.y. 3 = c. A.D. 1193 Registers the royal order remitting, on representation, certain taxes which the tāṇattār of the temple of Maṇōmayaṇīśvaram-Uđaiyār nāyanār had collected on the lands belonging to the temple and those of Mūlasthānam-Uđaiyanāyanār and Durgaiyār, and had thereby caused the stoppage of worship in them. Certain epigraphs (kalveṭtu) of the temple of Śrīmūlasthānam-Uđaiyār and the Durgaiyār placed near the northern entrance of this village having become obliterated, a tax, of 2 drummam on each mā of land was unjustly demanded on the dēvadāna lands of those temples, apparently by the king's officials and that on the representation made by two temple servants, the king cancelled the tax.

cells.reference: ARE, 1915, no. 582 ; Ibid. part II, para. 26.
cells.remarks: Records that as there was no money in the treasury of the temple of Piṇakkaṇutta-Nāyanār in Maliyadīkkuṣiṣchi, the southern hamlet of Pirāntaka-chaturvēdimaṅgalam a brahmadēya in Āri-nāđu, a certain Puliyūrkiļavaṇ Piraļaya-Viđaṅgaṇ, Abhayampukkāṇ living in the street called Kulasēkharapperunderu, defrayed the expenses to be met in regard to the tax callēd Viniyōgam on the tank Ulaguyya-vanda-Pāṇdyappērēri and made a gift of his right to one-third of the income from the tank along with some money to the temple, for offerings to Tiruppalļiyaṇai-Nāchchiyār and Tukkaiyār. Mentions the temple of Tirukkaļaniśvara-Mudaiya-Nāyanār at Savadampatṭakuṣiṣchi which belonged to the tantirattār i.e. the Kaikkōļas, the Sēnāpatis and Daṇdanāyakas.

cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xxx||236" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XXX, No. 236</button>
cells.remarks: Begins with introduction 'tirumalai-mādu' etc. Registers gift of tax free land as dēvadāna by Seṅgodikkuṇṇaṇ Sakrāyudan alias Vikrama Pāṇdyapaṇmaṇ of malai-maṇdalam, for the expenses of the temple of Piṇakkaṇuttiśvaram-Udaiyār at Malaiyaḍikkuṇchchi, which was the southern hamlet of the Parāntaka-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in Ārinādu. The gift was made under the orders of the king when he was in his palace at Alliyūr in Nāttāṇruppōkku at the request of his brother-in-law (machchāļvi) Vikrama-Chōladēva. It was stated that in assessing these lands and chaff, the others were to be charged at 7 Kalam of paddy on each mā of land 3/4 of this, on land on which the kuruvai paddy was grown ; a half on land grown with paddy sown in Tula ; lands growing gingili, varagu and tiṇai must be charged 1 diramam for 16 mā of land, and dry-croplands must be charged half diramam for each mā.

cells.remarks: States that while the king was seated in the throne called Muṇayadaruyan in the palace at Kuṛakkudi, Jātavēdabhatṭar of Mānābharaṇamangalam and Ponnanbhagavān alias Śrīvallabha-Kāṇāṭtuvēlāṇ represented to the king that an oil-mill may be installed and that a lamp may be maintained from the tax thereon (chekkiṛai) in the temple of Nichchitankaṇḍa viṇṇagarāyār in Teṇvārināḍu. Accordingly the king gave the necessary permission to set up the oil-mill from the 16th year. The document was signed by Ādivarāhap-Palla-varaiyan and Indramānap-pallavaraiyan.

cells.king: Jatāvarman alias Vira-Pāṇya (Vira Pāṇdya II ?) Vriśchika, 13, ba. di. shashti, Thursday and Aslesha, November 9
cells.reference: ARE, 1917, no. 432 ; Ibid., part II, para. 48, p. 155.
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction, tiruvaļarmulai, etc. Records that certain lands were purchased, by the village assembly from the Nagarattār of Sundara-Pāṇdyapuram in Kuṇumaṇai-nāđu for the temple of Tirukkuṇālam-uđaiya-Nāyanār and leased to Aṇđa-Piļai and his descendants on condition that he shall cultivate them and pay the taxes to the temple. It was stipulated that the lease would pay on every mā of waste plot that he brought under cultivation at the rate of 1 mā of achchu and 1 kalam of paddy for the first year, 2 mā of achchu and 2 kalam of paddy for the 2nd year, 3 mā of achchu and 3 kalam of paddy for the 3rd year and 4 mā of achchu and 4 kalam of paddy for the 4th and subsequent years.

The donor was a certain Udayadivākaraṇ Tirumūrti of Mādēvi-maṅgalam in Paṇaiyūmāđu in Kshatriyaśikhāmaṇi-valanāđu, a district in Chōlamaṇđalam.

The lampstand is described to have been cast with a woman’s figure holding a lamp.

cells.remarks: Commences with the historical introduction Tirumađandaiyum Jayamađandaiyum of the inscriptions of the king. Issued by the king when he was seated on his throne called Kaliṅgattaraiyaṇ in his palace at Madurai to the east of Māđakkulam. The first part of record states that at the request of his son (nampiļlai) Sundara-Pāndya, the lands in the village of Katṭānimaṅgalam which were in the possession of the temple of Māṇaviraviṇnagar-Āļvār in Māṇaviravaļanāđu were transferred to the temple of Vira-Pāndīśvaramuđaiyār as tax-free dēvadāna for different expenses of worship (Tiruppađimāřru). The second part of the inscription refers to the ulvari relating to the transaction.

cells.reference: : ARE, 1912, no. 26; SII. XIV, no. 16-A, pp. 12-17, EI., XXI, no. 17, pp. 101 ff.
cells.match: <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="are" data-key="are|1911-14|d|512" data-url="ARE-Inscriptions.html">ARE 1911-14, App. D, No. 26</button>; <button type="button" class="xref-link" data-corpus="sii" data-key="sii|xiv||16" data-url="SII-Inscriptions.html">SII Vol. XIV, No. 16</button>
cells.match_text: ARE 1911-14, App. D, No. 26; SII Vol. XIV, No. 16
cells.remarks: Records that the king made a gift of 1,400 paļaikāšu for meeting the various annual requirements of the temple of Subrahmaṇya-Bhatāra in the central shrine at Tiruchchendūr. The money was invested by the king's three officerss Iruppaikkuđi-Kiļavaṇ, Šāttamperumāṇ and Alaṛrūmāṭtukkōṇ with the administrative bodies of 16 villages which were required to pay annual interest in grain to the temple at two kalam per kāšu per year. Note : The inscription is important for determining the relative values of money, weights and measures prevalent in South India and furnished valuable data for reconstructing the economic conditions of the period. Niraimati-nārāyam is mentioned as a grain measure.

cells.remarks: The meykirtti portion beginning with pūmaruviya tirumaṭandaiyum, etc. enumerates the achievements of the king. On being crowned, the king is said to have sent a large army against the Chōla country to have set on fire Tañjai and Uṭandai, to have destroyed many tanks, rivers, and water sources, halls, fortifications, towers, theatres, mansions, palaces and pavillions, to have ploughed the enemy's country with asses, to have driven the Chōla king into the forest and to have taken away his crown. The victorious* Pāṇdya king is then said to have gone to Āyirattaṭi where he performed the anointment of heroes; to have entered the sacred city of Puliyūr, i.e. Chidambaram, and paid obeisance to Śiva; to have finally reached Ponnamaravati. While staying in Ponnamaravati the Pāṇdya king sent word to the Chōla promising to give back Chōnādu and the crown which he had lost. On hearing it, the Chōla returned with his wife, and presenting his legitimate son first, himself remaining behind, prostrated under the victorious lion-throne of the conqueror and begged. After removing the heat of Vaṭlavaṇ (i.e. the Chōla) caused by his flight and loss of territory with a libation of water, the Pāṇdya gave back to the Chōla king's legitimate son the crown and the expansive country. In support of this gift, he is also reported to have given a royal writ impressed with the fish seal, the title Chōlapati and his ancient city. The grant portions of the inscription inform us that in 20th year and 374th day of the king's reign, when he was pleased to remain on the reclining seat of Maṭlavarāyaṇ in the hall of the bedchamber of the palace at Tirunelvēli in Kiṭ-Vēmba-nādu, both the dēvakaṇmi of the temple of Tirunelvēli-uṭdaiyār and Saṅkaraṇ Aṭagiyapperumāṭ alias Maṭlavarāyaṇ of Kāladi, the Premier, made a request that certain lands of Kayattaṅkuṇchchi, which formed part of the jivita not only of the latter but also of his great grand-father Maṭlavarāyaṇ, who like him held the office of the Premier (Maṇṭalamudanmai) should be made tax-free and given to the temple to meet the expenses of offerings and worship to the image of Chokkanar which the Premier had caused to be set up in the temple, and the king complied with their requests.

cells.remarks: Records that, when the king was in his palace at Madurai in Māđukkuļakkiļ (East Māđakkuļam ?) in Maruruōdaya-vaļanāđu, 224 chaturvēdi-bhaṭtar, versed in the Vēdas and Sāstras and capable of expounding them, approached him and said that Kuđalūr in Murappu-nāđuand the villages comprised in Kīļai-Kuđalūr with the exclusion of 4 mā of land forming the palļichchanda as well as the old dēvadāna and the lands purchased by Udaiyaņ Kūrtāđuvāņ alias Villavadaraiyaņ of Vaļugūr residing in Kulasēkharap-perunteruvu at Paṭtiņa-Marudūr in šuraņguđi-nāđu and given as dēvadāna to the temple of Ulaguyyavanda-Ísvaram-uđaiyār might be constituted into a new village called Pōśala-vīra-Sōmidēva-chaturvēdimaņgalam after the name of the king's uncle (māmađi) and given as brahmadēya, divided into 244 shares, so that the 224 chaturvēdi-bhaṭtas mentioned above might have a share each, and 29 shares might be assigned to those that had to do service in the dēvadāna. As regards the assessment of the land of this new village, it is stated that the king's uncle enjoijed that the lands should be measured by the rod called Sundara-Pānđiyaņ-Kōl and 24 feet length the kind of crop raised should be examined, and for such of the land as had yielded produce, tax should be levied at the following rates, on each mā : (1) 1/4 kāśu for antarīya, viniyōga, achchu, kāriyavārāychchi, vettipāṭtam, pañchupili, sandhuvigrahappēru and all other payable dues, three kalam of paddy for kār crop ; (2) half of this rate shall be charged for lands sown in Tula and crops realised; (3) 2 tiramam shall be paid on lands on which varagu, tinaippul and Iru gu had been harvested; (4) for pāsanam the above rates should prevail.
